concept: Keyset pagination with compound sort keys
summary: Source-anchored research for Keyset pagination with compound sort keys. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: An ObjectId _id is not a strict clock: MongoDB notes that ObjectId values only have one second of temporal resolution, so values created within the same second have no guaranteed ordering, and they are generated by clients, which may have differing system clocks. For a consistent sort, include in the sort a field with unique values; _id is guaranteed unique, so adding it as a tie-breaker after a non-unique field such as a timestamp gives a consistent order. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort/

Keyset paging is less affected than offset paging by inserts or deletes before the current boundary because it anchors to values, but it is not snapshot-consistent. Concurrent changes or updates to mutable sort fields can make items appear twice or be missed. Prefer immutable sort fields and a unique tie-breaker when walking a changing collection. (medium confidence)

Use a compound index whose keys appear in the same order as the sort keys, with sort directions matching the index key pattern or its full inverse. An index can support a sort on a non-prefix subset only if the query has equality conditions on all the prefix keys that precede the sort keys. Inspect explain: in a reported case (SERVER-24027, MongoDB 3.2.3, fixed in 3.4.2), a multi-key $or pagination boundary with a descending compound sort produced an in-memory sort rather than a merge of index scans. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-24027

A compound lexicographic $or can still yield a poor plan. In one MongoDB case study, a find() predicate using a > cursorA OR (a == cursorA AND b > cursorB) with sort({a: 1, b: 1}) did not efficiently combine index filtering with ordered retrieval; the author used a staged aggregation to position near the cursor before applying the full boundary. This case report does not establish a general MongoDB limitation. (low confidence)

Treat the sort tuple as the cursor position. For sort {createdAt: -1, _id: -1}, the next-page boundary is createdAt < lastCreatedAt OR (createdAt == lastCreatedAt AND _id < lastId). For more keys, compare the first differing key after matching preceding keys for equality, using the comparison direction that matches that key's sort direction. (high confidence)

Sort fields that can tie need a unique final key to define a repeatable page boundary, often _id. MongoDB documents that tied sort keys can be returned in any relative order; MongoDB examples and implementations add _id after a timestamp or other paginated field. The unique tuple defines a deterministic order for a fixed dataset, but it does not create a snapshot across requests. (high confidence)

An indexed keyset (range) boundary lets queries use indexes to avoid scanning unwanted documents, so it typically scales better than skip() for deep sequential pages, because skip() must scan from the beginning of the result set. A literal multi-key $or boundary can plan poorly: in a reported case (SERVER-24027, MongoDB 3.2.3, fixed in 3.4.2/3.5.2), a descending compound-key $or pagination query fell back to an in-memory sort instead of a merge of index scans. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-24027
